predecessors.name: Kidarites
predecessors.text: Bactria, which the Alchons occupied around 370 'chasing the Kidarites toward India'

predecessors.name: Sasanian Empire
predecessors.text: Kabulistan, taken from the Sasanians around 380-385

successors.name: Turk Shahis (Kabul Shahi)
successors.text: Kabul and the Nezak country, replaced by the Turk Shahis around 665

successors.name: Western Turkic Khaganate (Western Göktürks)
successors.text: Gandhara, taken by the Western Turks in 625 (Yabghus of Tokharistan)

ledger.x: c. 370: the Alchons occupy Bactria. 'c. 370: Alchons occupied Bactria, chasing the Kidarites toward India, and minted coins imitating Shapur II'; infobox 'Established 370'.

c. 370: the Alchons chase the Kidarites toward India. The Alchon page has them ruling Gandhara 'alongside' the Kidarites around 380-385; the Kidarites dossier keeps Bactria as Kidarite land, so both claims are drawn as contested until the Kidarites fall in 467.

c. 380-385: the Alchons emerge at Kapisa. 'c. 380-385: Alchons emerged in Kapisa, taking Kabulistan from the Sassanians'; the page notes they are 'sometimes said' to have taken Kabul in 388. The year is the start of the span.

c. 430: Khingila takes the Hindu Kush routes. 'c. 430: Khingila emerged and took control of Hindu Kush routes from the Kidarites.' The page names routes, not land: Bamyan is the reading (confidence 1).
c. 450: the Hephthalites take Bactria. 'Hephthalites took Bactria around 450 CE, and later Nezak-Alchons took over parts of the region.' The White Huns dossier starts its Kunduz core in 450.
460-470: the Alchons take Gandhara and the Punjab.
467: the Kidarites fall.
470: the Alchons take the Punjab from the Guptas.
484: the Nezak branch takes Zabulistan.
496: the First Hunnic War begins.

c. 500: Toramana holds Malwa and Gujarat. '497-500: Kausambi was probably sacked before the Alchons occupied Malwa'; Toramana page 'conquest and control over Malwa and Gujarat' and 'His territory also included Uttar Pradesh, Rajasthan and Kashmir'. The year is the end of the span; Kashmir is left to 515.
Toramana holds Kashmir.
515: Prakashadharma defeats Toramana.
515: the rest of the Indian conquests go.
515: the First Hunnic War ends.
by 520: Mihirakula holds Sindh.
520: the Second Hunnic War begins and Mihirakula occupies north India.
c. 534: the Hunnic occupation ends. 'c. 534: The Second Hunnic War ended after about 15 years of occupation'; Yasodharman defeated Mihirakula at Sondani c. 528; Narasimhagupta Baladitya captured him.
by 542: the Punjab and Sindh are lost.

c. 560: the Sasanians and Western Turks may take Zabulistan. 'the Sasanians allied with the Western Turks against the Hephthalites, and they may have also wrestled control of Zabulistan from the Nezaks'. A maybe on the page: confidence 1.
625: the Western Turks take Gandhara.
c. 630: the Kashmir line of the Alchons ends. 'c. 590-630: Narendraditya Khinkhila ruled'; the infobox lists the Karkota dynasty among the successors but no page opened dates the handover.
670: the Alchon state ends.

wars.name: Alchon-Kidarite wars
wars.outcome: The Kidarites were chased toward India from c.

wars.name: Skandagupta's Huna war
wars.outcome: Skandagupta defeated an unnamed Huna ruler c.

wars.name: First Hunnic War
wars.outcome: Toramana reached the Alchon maximum, took Malwa and Gujarat, was beaten at Eran in 510 by Bhanugupta (Toramana page) and defeated by Prakashadharma in 515.

wars.name: Second Hunnic War
wars.outcome: About fifteen years of occupation; Yasodharman beat Mihirakula at Sondani (c.

wars.name: Hephthalite-Sasanian-Turk war
wars.outcome: The Hephthalites were defeated by the Sasanians and Western Turks (page: 557-565); the Sasanians may have taken Zabulistan.

wars.name: Arab invasions of Kabul
wars.outcome: An Arab army of about 6,000 in 654; Abd al-Rahman ibn Samura took Kabul after a siege in 665; a renewed offensive in 668.

certainty.note: A nomadic empire known from coins, seals and a few inscriptions (Eran, Risthal, Sanjeli); no page gives a border.
